issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a Developer instance method named swiftExperienceDescription(), but the solution defines the method as getExperienceDescription(). Additionally, the solution's Client.swift calls swiftExperienceDescription() while Developer.swift in the solution only provides getExperienceDescription(), causing a name mismatch that will prevent the code from compiling and confuses students about the required method name.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Rename the solution's getExperienceDescription() to swiftExperienceDescription(), and update all internal calls (including the initializer) to use swiftExperienceDescription(); or alternatively rename the template/problem references to match getExperienceDescription(). Ensure Client.swift, the Developer class, and the problem statement/template all use the same method name.

This mismatch (also visible as the solution's initializer calling getExperienceDescription while Client prints swiftExperienceDescription) creates a naming inconsistency that breaks the one-to-one mapping between the requirement and the implementation and can confuse students when locating/using the required method.

Rename getExperienceDescription() in the solution to swiftExperienceDescription(), and update all internal calls (the initializer print and any callers such as Client) to use swiftExperienceDescription() so names match the problem statement and template.
